title: Nidoqueen Has a Poison Safety Switch
premise: Nidoqueen’s back spines never secrete poison while young are nestled between them.
audiencePromise: See how Nidoqueen turns its most dangerous defense into a safe shelter for its young.
openLoop: Why would a Poison-type place its young between poisonous spines?
payoff: When young are present, Nidoqueen’s spines stop secreting poison and calm them safely.
engagementQuestion: Smart safety switch, or a dangerous design?

voice.instructions: Use a tense, curious pace. Stress safety switch, young, and no poison. Pause briefly before the final question.

scenes.headline: POISON HAS A SAFETY SWITCH
scenes.narration: Nidoqueen’s poison has one very specific safety switch.
scenes.caption: POISON HAS A SAFETY SWITCH

scenes.headline: YOUNG GO BETWEEN THE SPINES
scenes.narration: Nidoqueen places young in back gaps to pacify them.
scenes.caption: THE GAPS CALM ITS YOUNG

scenes.headline: THE SPINES SECRETE POISON
scenes.narration: With young present, the poison defense stays completely inactive.
scenes.caption: YOUNG PRESENT = NO POISON

scenes.headline: A SHELTER BETWEEN SPIKES
scenes.narration: The gaps pacify the young. With them present, spines never secrete poison.
scenes.caption: A CALM SHELTER BETWEEN SPIKES

scenes.headline: STRONGEST WHEN GUARDING
scenes.narration: And defending its young is when Nidoqueen is at its strongest.
scenes.caption: A CALM NEST, A FIERCE GUARD

scenes.headline: SMART SWITCH OR BAD DESIGN?
scenes.narration: Smart safety switch, or a dangerous design?
scenes.caption: SMART OR DANGEROUS?
